limitations: Saved actual tensor payloads exist only for out-of-tolerance updates; earlier comparisons are aggregate JSON evidence, not full actual snapshots.
Recorded private KV weights show received-cache support, not all per-update region allocation c>0 masks or all internal routing decisions.
A late threshold exceedance does not identify the operator where the original first gradient difference arose.
Second.bias common-score directions and Adam epsilon amplification are hypotheses requiring a controlled replay/intervention; this offline analysis does not establish causal attribution.
metric_notes: L2 relative errors are norm(reference-actual)/norm(reference); tensors use FP64 accumulation for norm reporting, while original FP32 torch.isclose remains the acceptance predicate.
Whole optimizer L2 includes step scalars and must not be interpreted as moment accuracy; per-moment errors are reported separately.
first_reference_bias_updates compares checkpoint257 against the original-owner reference258; it measures one trajectory update, not the reference-versus-restored difference.
Cache timestamps and weights for offending KV elements are included; their equality and positive support agreement do not establish all internal allocation support histories.
scope: CPU-only inspection of saved second-round Exchange-X recovery comparisons; no model execution or NPU initialization
